beats.text: Apollo's software lived on a chip.
beats.note: It lived in wire. Core rope memory stored the program by weaving wires through and around magnetic cores.

beats.text: A wire through a core meant a 1. A wire around it meant a 0.
beats.note: The software was physically woven into the memory.

beats.context: The size of the Apollo Guidance Computer's fixed memory, in six modules. Each word was 16 bits, 15 of data and one for parity.

beats.text: Women at Raytheon in Waltham, Massachusetts.
beats.note: Many were hired from the textile industry for their sewing skills. Others came from the Waltham Watch Company.

beats.text: About eight weeks and $15,000 for each module.
beats.note: Those are the figures given in a detailed technical write up.

beats.text: Once it was woven, the program could not be edited.
